text:
mohan: Quick follow-up — ran into an odd behaviour with the proxy-delegation flow during a contractor workload test. The proxy returned an org-scoped token instead of the expected project-scoped one and the job could access more than intended.

ada: ugh. can you paste the request/response headers (redact secrets) and the proxy routing rule?

mohan: sure — simplified:
```
POST /v1/tasks
Authorization: Bearer proxy-svc-token
X-Target-Project: proj-42
```
Proxy log: matched rule `delegate:org-default` -> minted token with scope `org:write` instead of `project:proj-42:run`

sara: is this the old fallback where proxy prefers broader scopes when it can't find an exact mapping? iirc we had that in the RFC as a降back behavior for multi-tenant proxies.

ada: yeah that fallback was deliberate to avoid denial during migrations, but it's dangerous for untrusted workloads (contractors). Should be opt-in.

ben: important point: we split trust boundaries — proxy identity vs end-actor identity. Proxy should never escalate above caller's declared intent. If we can't safely mint project-scoped token, we should fail, not mint org-scoped.

mohan: agree. we saw it because the mapping table lacked an explicit entry for proj-42 -> proxy-role binding so it used the default org binding.

ada: actionable options: 1) change default to deny (fail-fast), 2) keep allow but add a separate "broader-scope" opt-in flag per route, 3) audit + alert and leave behavior for now.

ben: my vote: (1) deny by default + a migration mode. Migration mode could be a header `X-Allow-Fallback: true` that is only toggled after manual review. Safer for security.

mohan: +1. We'll need a migration path for long-running batch jobs that relied on the fallback. Also, this touches token issuance metrics and monitoring.

ada: perf/ops note: deny-by-default will raise error rates during rollout. We should add explicit error classification so the console shows "delegation mapping missing" with remediation link.

sara: also need to plumb a different audit field: when proxy mints a broader token, log both requested and granted scopes and the rule id. Right now logs only show granted scope which hides the mismatch.

mohan: good catch. I'll open a quick PR to:
- change proxy default to deny for unresolvable mappings (config feature flag per deployment)
- add `X-Allow-Fallback` header for controlled rollout
- add detailed logging (`requested_scope`, `granted_scope`, `mapping_rule_id`)
- emit a metric `proxy.delegation.fallback` and an alert when >0.5% of requests use fallback for production services

ada: please add a short migration checklist in the PR describing steps for teams (audit usage, flip flag in staging, fix mapping table, flip in prod).

ben: small RFC follow-up: we should codify "fallback is never allowed for untrusted principals" — define untrusted = external/contractor/bot not in allowlist. That prevents this class of bugs.

mohan: noted. i'll add an entry to the authn/authz backlog and tag owners. will post PR link here when ready.

token-bot: Deploy-check: proxy-config-change requires canary rollout to infra-canary and 30m stable window.

ada: thanks. also @sara can you help with the logging schema so SIEM ingestion is clean?

sara: will do, i'll propose fields and event sample in the PR.

mohan: thanks everyone — short term: flip to deny-by-default behind feature flag. Long term: add allowlist and better mapping discovery tools.

ada: :thumbsup:
